decoys.summary: After an unmatched backtick opener populates the code-delimiter cache, later one-backtick openers can be closed by a cached two-backtick run. For example, prefix ``` unmatched `left``middle` tail ends the code span at the double backtick, exposing middle as ordinary Markdown instead of retaining left``middle in one code span.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify acceptance of a differently sized closing backtick run through the populated CodeDelims cache, and the resulting incorrect code-span boundary; a generic code-span or performance complaint does not match.

refutation.evidence: The cache is keyed by exact delimiter count: insert uses entry(count), and find reads only get_mut(&count). Its additional ix > open_ix guard prevents using a delimiter preceding the opener. The initial uncached scan also requires search_count == delim_count. The decoy_1_backtick_runs_match_exactly probe passed for both `left``middle` tail and prefix ``` unmatched `left``middle` tail. The latter first exhausts an unmatched triple-backtick opener and populates the cache. Both produce exactly one Code("left``middle") event, with tail outside the span. See controls_probe.rs:12 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

decoys.summary: With ENABLE_TABLES, inline code spans retain the backslash used to protect a table pipe. A body cell containing `a\|b` emits Code("a\|b") and renders a visible backslash, because make_code_span takes its content from the original source rather than the table-normalized inline text.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify retention of the table pipe-escape backslash inside an inline code span, yielding a\|b instead of a|b with ENABLE_TABLES. Ordinary backslashes outside tables or claims about unescaped pipes splitting cells do not match.

refutation.evidence: Although make_code_span starts from the raw source slice, its table-specific branch recognizes backslash followed by pipe, requires tree.is_in_table(), appends only the pipe, and advances by two bytes. The decoy_2_table_code_removes_pipe_escape probe passed: a two-column table containing `a\|b` emits Code("a|b"), retains exactly two cells per row, and renders a|b. The comparison outside a table emits the literal backslash, demonstrating that the table condition is active. See controls_probe.rs:25 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

false_findings.title: [P2] Preserve the first definition when reference labels are repeated
false_findings.body: A later reference definition overwrites the destination and title already stored for the same label during the block pass. Parsing [pick][id] followed by [id]: /first "First" and then [id]: /second "Second" therefore sends the earlier link to /second with title Second. CommonMark requires the first definition to win, so appending a duplicate definition silently retargets existing links. Keep the existing entry when a label is encountered again.

refutation.evidence: The insertion is entry(label).or_insert(link_def), which leaves an occupied entry unchanged. The false_1_first_reference_definition_wins probe passed for exactly the two definitions in the claim: reference_definitions().get("id") retains /first and First; parser events and rendered HTML also use /first and First. This directly disproves overwrite and retargeting. See controls_probe.rs:37 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

false_findings.title: [P2] Keep nested image endings from terminating the outer alt text
false_findings.body: The raw_text event consumer used for image alt attributes treats the end of a nested image as the end of the outer image. With ![before ![inner](small.png) after](image.png) tail, it closes the alt attribute after inner and renders the remaining after text outside the image. This loses part of the accessible description and leaks image-label content into the visible paragraph. The consumer needs to track nested start/end pairs before accepting an End as its terminator.

refutation.evidence: raw_text already tracks nesting: every Start increments nest; an End breaks only when nest == 0, otherwise it decrements nest and continues. The outer image Start has already been consumed by start_tag before raw_text is entered. The false_2_image_alt_consumes_nested_ends probe passed both the claimed nested-image input and an emphasis variant: each renders one image with alt="before inner after", followed only by the intended " tail". See controls_probe.rs:49 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

false_findings.title: [P1] Handle invalid Unicode scalar values in numeric entities without panicking
false_findings.body: The numeric-entity decoder assumes that a successfully parsed integer can be converted to a Unicode scalar value. Inputs such as � and � pass the digit and semicolon checks but fail character conversion, causing a panic while producing the text event. Ordinary Markdown can therefore terminate parsing instead of receiving the required replacement character. Handle the failed scalar conversion before constructing the entity text.

refutation.evidence:
char_from_codepoint uses fallible conversion and char::from_u32, returning Option. The numeric-entity branch explicitly calls unwrap_or(U+FFFD), so failed scalar conversion produces the replacement character without panicking. The false_3_invalid_numeric_entities_use_replacement_character probe passed for surrogate �, out-of-range �, decimal �, and �, each emitting U+FFFD and rendering

U+FFFD

followed by a newline. The valid upper boundary 􏿿 remains U+10FFFF. See controls_probe.rs:60 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

false_findings.title: [P2] Accept autolinks with a 32-character URI scheme
false_findings.body: The URI autolink scanner includes the colon in its scheme-length counter and rejects the inclusive upper boundary. An angle-bracket autolink consisting of 32 ASCII a characters followed by :item, such as <aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa:item>, is emitted as literal text instead of a LinkType::Autolink event. CommonMark permits schemes of up to 32 characters, so the length check drops valid links at that boundary. Adjust the check to account for the consumed colon.

refutation.evidence: The loop increments i before matching the colon, so i is scheme length plus one. The existing accepted range is 3..=33, correctly corresponding to scheme lengths 2..=32. The false_4_autolink_scheme_inclusive_upper_boundary probe passed: lengths 2, 31, and 32 produce Autolink events with the complete destination and matching anchor HTML; length 33 does not produce an autolink. The exact 32-a trigger in the finding is included. See controls_probe.rs:71 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.

false_findings.title: [P2] Do not terminate bare link destinations at an inner closing parenthesis
false_findings.body: The non-angle-bracket destination scanner stops at the first closing parenthesis even when that parenthesis belongs to a balanced pair inside the URL. For [label](a(b)c) tail, the link destination is truncated to a(b and the remaining c) is emitted as paragraph text. This breaks valid Markdown links containing parenthesized path components. Consume balanced inner parentheses before treating a closing parenthesis as the inline-link terminator.

refutation.evidence: The bare-destination branch maintains nest, incrementing it on each opening parenthesis. A closing parenthesis breaks the loop only when nest == 0; otherwise it decrements nest and is included in the scanned destination. The caller then consumes the separate outer closing parenthesis. The false_5_balanced_parentheses_stay_in_link_destination probe passed for both [label](a(b)c) tail and [label](a(b(c)d)e) tail: destinations are exactly a(b)c and a(b(c)d)e, and the only text after each link is " tail". See controls_probe.rs:85 and probes.log under /work/prepared/evidence.
